title: Hibernate laptops on critical battery once hibernation is set up
head: 28c4d460757b
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Existing hibernating laptops do not receive the critical-battery policy on upgrade
leads.consequence: The default file is packaged under /usr/share/omarchy/default, but neither a package install nor any new migration invokes setup or copies it to /etc/UPower. A laptop already configured for hibernation continues using its prior UPower action/thresholds indefinitely, unless its owner manually reruns hibernation setup. The special already-configured branch only helps when that manual rerun happens.

leads.summary: Battery detection skips UPower-supported laptops with non-BAT names or no present attribute
leads.consequence: The new guard treats a system battery such as the Snapdragon qcom-battmgr-bat as a desktop, returning successfully without writing the drop-in. The existing helper also excludes a legitimate battery lacking a readable present file, which UPower itself treats as present. These machines keep Auto and 2% despite UPower managing their real battery. PR #13029 separately documents the Snapdragon name and proposes changing the helper; this feature should either use its corrected predicate or handle those shapes itself.
leads.triage: dropped: pre-existing helper limit (BAT* names), handled by open #13029; Opus noted privately

leads.summary: A valid existing PercentageLow override can make UPower discard both new thresholds
leads.consequence: UPower validates PercentageLow > PercentageCritical > PercentageAction, but the drop-in changes only the latter two. For a previously valid local PercentageLow=8 (and Critical=5, Action=2) in the main file or an earlier drop-in, the merged 8/8/5 configuration fails validation and UPower resets the whole trio to stock 20/5/2. Hibernate is then attempted at 2%, exactly the too-late threshold this PR aims to replace. A user's UsePercentageForPolicy=false also deliberately uses TimeAction instead of the new percentage. Validate the effective trio or include a compatible low threshold without silently defeating legitimate user choices.
leads.triage: dropped: needs a user-customised PercentageLow; stock 20 passes (Opus verified)

leads.summary: A failed drop-in install is reported as successful hibernation setup
leads.consequence: If mkdir or mktemp/install/mv fails (for instance sudo fails, source file missing or disk full), the helper prints an error but its else branch ends in a successful echo. Neither caller checks the failure, and the script has no set -e: on the already-configured path it prints 'Hibernation is already set up' and exits 0; on the fresh path it continues to rebuilding and optional reboot. The protection remains absent and a later automated retry is not scheduled. Return failure from the helper and make both callers report it without announcing success.
leads.triage: dropped: Opus judged exit 0 on install failure acceptable (installer must not fail)

leads.summary: Fresh setup activates the new battery policy before hibernation is reboot-ready
leads.consequence: On first setup, the drop-in is written and the running UPower daemon restarted at line 171, before the UKI rebuild at 179 and before any requested reboot at 183. If the rebuild fails, --no-rebuild's caller fails to complete boot preparation, or the user delays rebooting into the new image, a 5% UPower event can request Hibernate while the installed boot image still lacks the new resume configuration. The new early exit also trusts the resume-hook file alone rather than checking a bootable resume path. Consider enabling/restarting the action only once resume is operational, or document the pending-reboot and failed-rebuild window.
leads.triage: sent to Opus (followup-1.md): window pre-exists at base and opens earlier there; not material; dropped

leads.summary: Removing hibernation can leave a critical Hibernate override installed when its marker is missing
leads.consequence: When the resume hook was removed separately, changed/malformed, or a partial repair cleared it while leaving the UPower drop-in, the new cleanup is unreachable: remove prints 'Hibernation is not set up' and exits 0 before looking for the drop-in. UPower continues to request Hibernate at 5%, even though the resume setup is absent. Remove the Omarchy-owned drop-in on that early-exit path as well, subject to user confirmation and ownership checks.
leads.triage: dropped: edge case already in Opus private minor notes

leads.summary: The new test can pass without running and never covers first-time setup or effective thresholds
leads.consequence: Line 11 returns success with SKIP on any environment lacking /sys/power/image_size, though the stubbed early-branch file operations need no real hibernation hardware. Where it does run, every setup call has a preseeded resume marker, so deleting the fresh-setup installation call at setup:171 would not fail the test. Likewise a shipped PercentageCritical=25.0 (invalid above stock Low=20) passes its cmp and Hibernate grep yet causes UPower to reset thresholds. Add a hardware-independent first-setup fixture and assertions for all effective policy values; retain the existing rerun/remove checks.
leads.triage: corroborates first-setup and sysfs-skip optional note; threshold-assertion sub-point dropped as nitpick

leads.summary: PR #13610 is a divergent implementation of this same target and does not merge cleanly
leads.consequence: Both PRs install to /etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf. #13610's setup uses a different default source path, helper and failure semantics, and also adds an automatic migration. Read-only compare API reports diverged; merging setup against the shared unchanged script gives three unresolved conflict hunks. Remove's textual merge succeeds but contains two separately named cleanup blocks for the same path (the second normally skips after the first removed it). Choose one source file/helper implementation and reconcile the migration when one PR lands, rather than merging both policies unexamined.
leads.triage: corroborates #13610 note; self-check refined to conflict in setup only

leads.summary: Setup overwrites and remove deletes a user's own policy edits to the Omarchy-named drop-in
leads.consequence: A user tuning the installed /etc drop-in's thresholds or action will have edits overwritten verbatim the next time setup is rerun; remove deletes the file even if its content is no longer Omarchy's. A user with a custom CriticalPowerAction in the main UPower.conf or an earlier drop-in also has that explicit choice overridden by this 70-* entry. No prior configuration is backed up/restored, so after removal the effective policy may not be the prior stock default. Preserve edited installed content or ask before replacement and make the override explicit in docs.
leads.triage: dropped: user edits of an Omarchy-owned drop-in, low value

leads.summary: Hibernation manual does not disclose the new automatic 5% action
leads.consequence: The manual still describes setting up hibernation as exposing a menu entry, without saying that running the command now opts every detected laptop into an automatic Hibernate at UPower's 5% action threshold, changes its critical level to 8%, and supersedes earlier UPower.conf custom action settings. Readers cannot make an informed choice about the behaviour until battery drain triggers it. Document the policy, conditions and override path with the setup instructions.
leads.triage: verified directly (manual/36-system-sleep.md:15-19); published as optional note

limits: No PR scripts, test cases, system services or package builds executed; all behavioral findings are traced from pinned source and UPower v1.91.3 source. Conditional runtime outcomes (battery discharge and resume) require a safe hardware lab to demonstrate physically.

Related PR merges other than #13610 were inspected for overlapping target and scope but not validated as merged builds; other PRs may change before review completes.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** Laptops that already have hibernation keep the old critical battery action after updating.

### Existing hibernating laptops keep the 2% default

Only setup installs the drop-in, and nothing in `bin/`, `install/` or `migrations/` reruns it after an update. **Impact:** the laptops in #13256 keep `CriticalPowerAction=Auto` at 2% unless setup is rerun by hand.

**Suggested change:** add a migration that installs it when `omarchy_resume.conf` has `HOOKS+=(resume)` and `omarchy-battery-present` succeeds, with setup's `cmp` check and `try-restart`.

<details><summary>Reproducer (source search at 28c4d460)</summary>

# Reproducer: laptops that already have hibernation keep the stock critical action after updating

Reviewed head: 28c4d460757bb037ef99fe3fd67912cccef5c36c.

This is a source-level reproduction: it shows that nothing in the update path installs the new drop-in, so an existing install only gets it if the user reruns `omarchy hibernation setup` by hand.

The installer sets hibernation up as a fixed install phase: `configure_hibernation` in omacom/omarchy-iso (listed in `orchestrator/main.py`, defined in `configs/airootfs/usr/share/omarchy-iso/orchestrator/phases_impl.py`, public branch `quattro` at 86c07785) runs `arch-chroot <target> env OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy ... /usr/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup --force --no-rebuild` (setup itself exits early where the kernel has no hibernation support). Laptops installed this way therefore already have `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf`, which sends a rerun down the already-configured branch. Nothing on the update path in `bin/`, `install/` or `migrations/` reruns setup or installs the drop-in; the only other caller is factory reset, as the searches below show.

From a checkout of the PR head:

```bash
rg -n "omarchy-hibernation-setup" bin install migrations
rg -n "critical-hibernate|UPower.conf.d" bin install migrations
```

Actual output:

```
bin/omarchy-system-factory-reset:262:  if [[ -x $next/usr/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup ]] && grep -q "/swap/swapfile" "$next/etc/fstab"; then
bin/omarchy-system-factory-reset:278:      /usr/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup --force --no-rebuild >>"$LOG_FILE" 2>&1; then

bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup:32:UPOWER_DROP_IN="/etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf"
bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup:67:  cmp -s "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/upower/omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf" "$UPOWER_DROP_IN" && return 0
bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup:71:  if install_root_file "$OMARCHY_PATH/default/upower/omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf" "$UPOWER_DROP_IN" 0644; then
bin/omarchy-hibernation-remove:48:UPOWER_DROP_IN="/etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf"
```

The only caller of `omarchy-hibernation-setup` in shipped code (`bin/`, `install/`, `migrations/`) is factory reset, and no migration mentions the drop-in. On an existing hibernating laptop, UPower keeps the stock `CriticalPowerAction=Auto` with `PercentageAction=2.0` after the update that ships this PR.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (UPower 1.91.4 and systemd 262 source, sandbox runs):
- `70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf` matches UPower's `conf.d` name pattern and loads after `UPower.conf`, whose stock copy defines all three keys the drop-in overrides.
- With the stock `PercentageLow=20`, 20 > 8 > 5 passes UPower's ordering check.
- When logind's `CanHibernate` is not `yes`, UPower falls back to PowerOff.
- Rerunning setup is idempotent (no restart when the file is unchanged), machines without a battery get nothing, and remove deletes the file and restarts UPower.
- The PR's test fails at the base commit and catches removal of the rerun call, the battery gate, the `cmp` guard, the install-path restart and the remove block.

**Optional notes:**
- **Optional test improvement:** the test only reruns setup with the resume marker present, so deleting the first-setup call at `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup:171` (the path new installs take) leaves all five checks passing; the first-setup case in the next block catches it. The test also skips wherever `/sys/power/image_size` is absent. Redirecting `/sys/power/` in `redirect()`, creating a stand-in `image_size` in the scratch root and dropping the host skip let all five checks run and pass in a sandbox without it.
- Open PR #13610 installs the same destination file with the same values, adds a migration and edits the same parts of `omarchy-hibernation-setup`, so the two PRs conflict there.
- `manual/36-system-sleep.md` does not mention that hibernation setup now changes the critical battery action; a sentence there would tell users about it (the drop-in is `/etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf`).
</details>

<details><summary>Reproducer for the first-setup test (fails at 28c4d460 with line 171 removed)</summary>

# Reproducer: the first-setup path is not covered by the PR's test

Reviewed head: 28c4d460757bb037ef99fe3fd67912cccef5c36c (base 97a9fce5).

New installs reach `setup_critical_battery_hibernate` through the first-setup path (the installer runs `omarchy-hibernation-setup --force --no-rebuild`), at `bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup` line 171. `test/shell.d/hibernation-critical-battery-test.sh` only runs setup on an already-configured machine, so removing that call leaves the whole file green.

## Step 1: remove the first-setup call and run the PR's test

From a checkout of the PR head, on a machine where `/sys/power/image_size` exists (the test skips otherwise):

```bash
sed -i '/^setup_critical_battery_hibernate$/d' bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup
bash test/shell.d/hibernation-critical-battery-test.sh
```

The edit removes exactly one line:

```diff
@@ -168,7 +168,6 @@
   fi
 fi
 
-setup_critical_battery_hibernate
 
 if ! $NO_REBUILD; then
```

Actual output, exit status 0 (run in a sandbox with a private `/sys/power/image_size` stand-in):

```
ok - rerunning setup on a laptop installs the critical battery hibernate action
ok - the critical battery action is Hibernate, not suspend-then-hibernate
ok - an installed action is left alone
ok - a machine without a battery gets no battery action
ok - removing hibernation removes the critical battery action
```

## Step 2: a test case for the first-setup path

Save as `test/shell.d/hibernation-critical-battery-first-setup-test.sh` (the PR's sudo stub and /etc and /swap redirection, plus btrfs, swaplabel and swapon stubs and a redirected system-sleep directory):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#
# The first hibernation setup on a laptop (the installer runs it with --force
# --no-rebuild) also installs the critical battery action. /etc, /swap and the
# system-sleep hook directory are redirected into a scratch root; sudo runs the
# file operations there and records service restarts.

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

[[ -f /sys/power/image_size ]] || { skip "no hibernation support to exercise"; exit 0; }

scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$scratch/bin" "$scratch/etc/limine-entry-tool.d" "$scratch/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep" "$scratch/swap"
export CALL_LOG="$scratch/calls"
export OMARCHY_PATH="$ROOT"
export PATH="$scratch/bin:$ROOT/bin:$PATH"

cat > "$scratch/bin/sudo" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1" in
  systemctl) echo "systemctl ${*:2}" >> "$CALL_LOG" ;;
  /usr/bin/install)
    args=()
    while (($# > 1)); do
      shift
      case "$1" in -o | -g) shift ;; *) args+=("$1") ;; esac
    done
    exec /usr/bin/install "${args[@]}"
    ;;
  *) exec "$@" ;;
esac
STUB
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' > "$scratch/bin/omarchy-battery-present"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "btrfs $*" >> "$CALL_LOG"\n' > "$scratch/bin/btrfs"
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' > "$scratch/bin/swaplabel"
printf '#!/bin/bash\necho "%s"\n' "$scratch/swap/swapfile" > "$scratch/bin/swapon"
chmod +x "$scratch/bin/"*

sed -e "s|/etc/|$scratch/etc/|g" -e "s|\"/swap|\"$scratch/swap|g" \
  -e "s|/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/|$scratch/usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/|g" \
  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-hibernation-setup" > "$scratch/omarchy-hibernation-setup"

# Swap subvolume, swapfile, fstab entry and resume parameters already exist, so
# the run only writes the resume hook, the sleep hook and the battery action.
printf '\n# Btrfs swapfile for system hibernation\n%s none swap defaults,pri=0 0 0\n' "$scratch/swap/swapfile" > "$scratch/etc/fstab"
echo 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=/dev/null resume_offset=1"' > "$scratch/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf"

: > "$CALL_LOG"
bash "$scratch/omarchy-hibernation-setup" --force --no-rebuild > "$scratch/out" 2>&1 ||
  fail "first setup on a laptop succeeds" "$(<"$scratch/out")"
grep -qx 'HOOKS+=(resume)' "$scratch/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf" ||
  fail "first setup writes the resume hook" "$(<"$scratch/out")"
cmp -s "$ROOT/default/upower/omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf" \
  "$scratch/etc/UPower/UPower.conf.d/70-omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf" ||
  fail "first setup on a laptop installs the critical battery action" "$(<"$scratch/out")"
grep -qx 'systemctl try-restart upower.service' "$CALL_LOG" || fail "UPower is restarted to read the new action"
pass "first setup on a laptop installs the critical battery action"
```

Actual results (same sandbox):

At the PR head, unmodified (exit 0):

```
ok - first setup on a laptop installs the critical battery action
```

At the PR head with the Step 1 edit (exit 1):

```
Adding resume hook to <scratch>/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf
not ok - first setup on a laptop installs the critical battery action
```

At the base commit 97a9fce5, with the PR's `default/upower/omarchy-critical-hibernate.conf` copied in (exit 1):

```
Adding resume hook to <scratch>/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf
not ok - first setup on a laptop installs the critical battery action
```

`<scratch>` replaces the test's own `mktemp -d` scratch root, redacted from the output; nothing else in the output is changed.
</details>
